newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia firm signs $480 mln loan for phone lines.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia firm signs $480 mln loan for phone lines.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Mitra Global Telekomunikasi Indonesia said it had signed a deal on Tuesday to secure a $480 million syndicated loan to develop 400,000 telephone lines in Central Java and Jogjakarta.

Mitra is owned by Indonesia's state-controlled satellite operator PT Indonesia Satelit Corporation (Indosat), Australia's Telstra Global Limited, Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and Japan's Itochu Corp.
"The loan amounts to $480 million for a period of 9.5 years, with a competitive rate of 1.35 percent above LIBOR," Mitra said in a statement.
It said the lead arrangers for the syndicated loan were Australia and New Zealand Banking Group, Japan's Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd and Deutsche Bank AG's Deutsche Bank Asia Pacific.
Mitra's president director SWS Hardjito said in the statement that the development of the 400,000 telephone lines was expected to be completed in March 1999.
